newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke warns against EMU failure.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke warns against EMU failure.

text.p: Bundesbank council members Ernst Welteke said on Monday that the risk of failure to establish a single currency in Europe is greater than any of the risks involved with monetary union itself.
"The biggest risk is in the collapse of the plan," Welteke told an audience of tourism industry officials.
Only those nations that meet the tough fiscal criteria for entry into European economic and monetary union (EMU) in 1999 should be allowed to join from the start, Welteke said.
He said there was little chance of delaying the beginning of EMU so it would behoove all potential members to quickly prepare to meet the budget targets restricting deficits and public debt.
"Another significant risk is the question how wide the circle of nations participating in EMU will be and whether nations who aren't fit to join and could therefore threaten stability," he said.
As a counter measure to ensure lasting stability, it was imperative that a stability pact with sanctions for countries that break fiscal discipline should be adopted.
Welteke said he expected some compromise to be made between currently conflicting positions on the stability pact before the December European Union summit in Dublin.
Welteke warned that if EMU did not proceed as planned protectionism in Europe would increase and exchange rates would again become turbulent.
As key benefit of the currency union, Welteke named the calming of otherwise volatile currency markets in Europe, which will particularly benefit German exporters.
European travellers will benefit from the fact that prices will be immediately comparable throughout Europe.
